summary: While adding an options check in pretty-ms, the user asks for error messages to start with the package name ('pretty-ms: Expected ...') in all of his packages, because their log collector drops stack traces. The last session is in parse-ms, whose code uses plain 'Expected ...' messages; the task adds a `largestUnit` option that throws a TypeError for bad values. A no-memory agent copies parse-ms's existing message style.

turns: People keep calling prettyMilliseconds(ms, 2) thinking the second argument is unitCount, and it gets silently ignored. Make it throw a TypeError when options is passed but isn't an object. Add a test.

Can you start the error messages with the package name, like 'pretty-ms: Expected …'? I want that in all my packages: a lot of our logs come through a collector that drops stack traces, and then I can't tell which dependency threw. Change the existing one too.

Let's add a `largestUnit` option to parseMilliseconds: 'days' (the default), 'hours', 'minutes' or 'seconds'. Bigger units roll into it, so {largestUnit: 'hours'} gives hours: 26 instead of days: 1, hours: 2. It should work for bigint input too, and throw a TypeError for any other value. Add tests.

facts.text: In all of the user's packages, error messages start with the package name (e.g. 'pretty-ms: Expected …'), because their log collector drops stack traces.
